claim: The 2025 MICHELIN Guide Vietnam awarded Hanoi three one-star restaurants (Gia, Hibana by Koki, Tam Vi), one Green Star (Lamai Garden), plus Bib Gourmand and Selected entries; no 2026 Vietnam guide has been issued yet.
quote: The 2025 MICHELIN Guide Hanoi | Ho Chi Minh City | Da Nang Celebrates Vietnam's Culinary Ascent with 9 One Star, 2 Green Star, and 63 Bib Gourmand

claim: Hibana by Koki is a one-Michelin-star 14-seat teppanyaki counter in the basement of Capella Hanoi, 11 Le Phung Hieu Street, with premium ingredients (abalone, spiny lobster, sea urchin, Hokkaido hairy crab, Kyori beef) flown in from Japan.
quote: Guests are cosseted from start to finish during this theatrical dining experience at the 14-seat counter in the Capella Hanoi hotel basement. Affable Chef Hiroshi Yamaguchi skilfully cooks teppanyaki dishes that are rich and complex in flavour.

claim: Tam Vi, one Michelin star, sits at 4B Yen The Street, Dong Da and serves traditional Northern Vietnamese dishes like cha oc (ham with periwinkle snails) and clear crab-malabar spinach soup in a rustic-antique setting.
quote: Highlights include cha oc (ham with periwinkle snails) served with herbs, vegetables, vermicelli and fish sauce, and the subtle crab soup with malabar spinach in a clear broth.

claim: T.U.N.G dining (Twisted, Unique, Natural, Gastronomique) is a Michelin Guide-listed fine-dining tasting-menu restaurant near St. Joseph's Cathedral and Hoan Kiem Lake led by chef Hoang Tung; it has appeared in the Guide 2023-2025 but holds no star.
quote: T.U.N.G dining is nestled in the heart area of Hanoi, a few steps away from St. Joseph's Cathedral and Hoan Kiem lake. The 4-letter name stands for Twisted, Unique, Natural, Gastronomique.

claim: Hanoi's 2025 Michelin lineup: Gia (61 Van Mieu, signatures Phu Quoc herring porridge and crab spring rolls); Bib Gourmand picks Ha Thanh Mansion, Mau Dich So 37, Mien Luon Chan Cam, Pho Bo Lam, Uu Dam (vegetarian); Selected entries Vien Dining, Pho Tien, Pho Cuon Chinh Thang.
quote: Gia - Cuisine: Modern Vietnamese - Address: 61 Van Mieu Street ... Signature: Phu Quoc herring porridge, reinvented crab spring rolls ... Ha Thanh Mansion ... Mau Dich So 37 ... Mien Luon Chan Cam ... Pho Bo Lam ... Uu Dam ... Vien Dining ... Pho Tien ... Pho Cuon Chinh Thang

claim: Sofitel Legend Metropole Hanoi houses Le Beaulieu (French fine dining; lunch, dinner, Sunday brunch), Spices Garden (elevated Vietnamese; lunch and dinner) and La Terrasse (French sidewalk-cafe style; all day) — note La Maison 1888 is in Da Nang, not Hanoi.
quote: Le Beaulieu - Cuisine: French fine dining - Meals: Lunch, dinner, Sunday brunch ... Spice Garden - Cuisine: Vietnamese (elevated) - Meals: Lunch, dinner ... La Terrasse - Cuisine: French cafe-inspired - Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner

claim: Le Beaulieu's Sunday Brunch at Sofitel Metropole Hanoi runs noon-3:30pm and costs VND 2,500,000++ per person (about US$100), with wine/champagne options to VND 4,500,000++, served with live jazz and a buffet of fresh seafood, foie gras, lobster bisque and Serrano ham.
quote: The Sunday Brunch costs VND 2,500,000++ per person, with wine options at VND 3,500,000++ per person or VND 4,500,000++ per person with wine and champagne ... The brunch runs from 12 till 3:30pm on Sundays.

claim: Cau Go Vietnamese Cuisine occupies floors 6-7 of 9 Dinh Tien Hoang, Hoan Kiem, with a 7th-floor terrace overlooking Hoan Kiem Lake, and has been in the Michelin Guide for three consecutive years serving regional Vietnamese fare.
quote: Cau Go Vietnamese Cuisine is set above the historic Cau Go Street and overlooks Hoan Kiem Lake. The restaurant is located at 6-7F, 9 Dinh Tien Hoang Street ... The restaurant is recognized in the Michelin Guide for three consecutive years.

claim: Madame Hien, opened in 2008 by French chef Didier Corlou in a yellow colonial villa in the Old Quarter, serves traditional Vietnamese dishes (banh cuon, pho, nem, com nieu, grilled suckling pig, lemongrass-duck foie gras) as a tribute to his Vietnamese grandmother-in-law.
quote: Madame Hien Restaurant is located in the heart of Hanoi's Old Quarter, housed in a charming yellow colonial villa. Opened since 2008 by celebrated French chef Didier Corlou, the establishment is a tribute to his Vietnamese grandmother-in-law.

claim: Hibana by Koki offers an omakase lunch from about VND 1.7 million (~US$65) per person, making it the most affordable Michelin-starred meal in Vietnam.
quote: Hibana by Koki offers an omakase lunch from around VND 1.7 million (around 65 USD) per person, making it the most affordable Michelin-starred option in the country.
